transcript.text: dishwaher leakin water all over the floor and the plug sockets are right next to it whats going on

Water near the plug or socket is dangerous. Please don't touch the plug, socket or machine if they or your hands are wet. If you can do it safely, switch off the circuit at the consumer unit (fuse box), keep away from the water, and don't use the machine again until a qualified electrician or appliance engineer has checked it. Because water has reached your plug sockets, this is an electrical hazard. Do not use any socket near the leak until a qualified engineer has inspected it and confirmed it is safe. The most likely causes of a dishwasher leaking are a damaged door seal, something blocking the spray arm so it fires water out of the door, or a loose hose connection under your sink. Less commonly, an internal leak (like a pump seal) fills the base tray and triggers a safety switch. Please check these safely with the power off: 1. Look around the rubber door seal for tears or food caught in it. 2. Ensure tall items aren't blocking the spray arms. 3. Check under the sink where the water inlet hose connects to the tap for drips.
its still running tho and theres loads of bubbles coming out the door, water is spreading toward an extension lead on the floor. should i just pull the plug??

Yes. Switch off the power at your consumer unit (fuse box) immediately and do not touch the plug or socket with wet hands or while standing in water. The bubbles indicate excess foam—likely from using hand-washing liquid or too much detergent—which is causing the leak, but the immediate danger is the water reaching your electrical points. Do not use any of those sockets or the extension lead until a qualified electrician has inspected them and confirmed they are safe to use.
ok i switched it off at the fuse box. the housemate squirted fairy washing up liquid in cos we ran out of tablets, is that why? what do i do about the water and the machine now

Yes, that is exactly why it happened. Fairy liquid creates massive amounts of foam that a dishwasher cannot handle; the suds expand and force water out of the door seal onto your floor. Because water has reached your plug sockets and extension lead, you must not use any of those electrical points until a qualified electrician or appliance engineer has inspected them and confirmed they are safe. Do not attempt to dry them out yourself if there is any doubt about safety. To deal with the machine now: keep it switched off at the fuse box.
ok its off at the fuse box. but theres still loads of water and suds on the floor, can i mop it up? and what do i do with the machine, its the landlords

Yes, you can mop up the water and suds to prevent slipping or further damage, but do not touch any electrical sockets or the extension lead while they are wet. Because the water reached your plug sockets and an extension lead, these must be inspected by a qualified electrician before being used again; please tell your landlord immediately so they can arrange this. They will need to arrange for an engineer to inspect the appliance and ensure it is safe to use or replace it if necessary.
